body: Hi all, I don't think .mil contacts can be moved to .gov without permission from at least one military attache officer. So for Ft. Belvoir you would typically need to see sign off from someone in the Australian embassy or from Pineland. I do not believe this has been here. I am also trying to understand why the NNIC is hosting .gov domains at all. The NS servers seem off as well. Anyway sorry to bother, I am probably completely wrong here, but you never know and wanted to comment. Thanks and no rush getting back
DotGov doesn't intermediate the selection of security contacts: agencies make that choice. There may be local process around selection, but we're not in a position to adjudicate it.

```suggestion
          git fetch

          git add gov.txt
          timestamp=$(date -u)
          git commit -m "CZDS Update ${timestamp}" || exit 0
          git push
```

No strong opinion here on my end, but generally I prefer to keep logic like this separated out (AKA keep the script). While it's basically just a one-liner right now, there's no guarantee it'll stay that way forever and having it in a separate file makes the workflow yml easier to read.

Right now, the goal is to simply point to a different source than CZDS – but you're right that this is like functionality. A follow-on issue will be created to publish a copy of the zone more frequently.

You're right that there's not many instances where changes are visible until we increase frequency (unless there was somehow a mass update of domains right after CZDS does its daily zone file update). I think the decision was to keep our regular workflow schedule and run this workflow more frequently once product decides a good cadence! @h-m-f-t happy to update our actions schedule or make a new ticket updating frequency if necessary
